Chris-sulzbach-avatar-render.jpg|link=https://tomato-kale-ngzb.squarespace.com/work/xcom2-advent The Avatar is an alien enemy encountered in XCOM 2. They are the ultimate goal of the Avatar Project, led by the ADVENT occupation on Earth: a new series of bodies for the Elders that are far healthier than their decaying Ethereal ones, and exponentially more powerful psionically. While very powerful, the Avatars encountered in game are incomplete; without the entirety of the Avatar Project, their bodies are not nearly as potent as a completed Avatar is presumed to be.

Units in XCOM 2 have 2 Action Points per turn, some actions (like shooting or dashing without specific abilities) use up both actions at once. Some actions like Grapple with the grappling hook are a free action that do not use up. Abilities like psi operatives Inspire give additional Action Points. Skirmisher skill Marauder lets Skirmishers shoot as a single action allowing them to shoot twice or move after shooting. (Was there another skill like this?)

Operation Devil's Moon is a mission for XCOM: Enemy Unknown. This unique mission serves as a tutorial for new players and, unlike normal missions in the game, is entirely scripted; the soldiers, enemies and overall outcome are always the same (including the death of three of the squad members). This mission takes place in a random city in Germany (Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg, or Munich); the mission is the same in all cities.
A Power Generator is a facility in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. It serves as the basic power production facility.
The Hover S.H.I.V. is a weapon platform in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. It is an upgraded version of the Alloy S.H.I.V. that has the ability to fly.

Frostbite is an ability introduced in the Alien Hunters DLC for XCOM 2. It is unique to the Serpent Suit. When activated, the soldier launches their Grappling Hook at a target, freezing it. Humanoid targets (like ADVENT troops) will be pulled out of cover into the open. Frostbite is a free action, and has a single charge per mission. It has a certain percent chance to hit, unlike other armor abilities. If Frostbite misses, it has a 2 turn cooldown before it can be used again.
Range is a parameter which may refer to the distance and/or the radius of an attack or ability. Attacks and abilities may have both range (distance) and effect radius (e.g. blast radius, AOE area).

The Sniper Class is a soldier class in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. The primary role of the Sniper Class is providing long range standoff, force multiplier and supporting Overwatch against enemy units. Their ability to precisely place a round where needed greatly enhances the survivability of the squad, reduces collateral damage, and increases mission success.
Telekinetic Field is an ability of the Psionic Class in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

Shieldwall is an ability granted by the W.A.R. Suit. The wearer of the W.A.R. Suit becomes a piece of full cover wherever they stand: "Provide high cover to squadmates wherever you stand. Moving or attacking will cancel the effect." Both allies and enemies may take advantage of this cover. If an ally already has high cover from an enemy, careful use of the Shieldwall ability may break the enemy's line of sight to that trooper. Moving or attacking will cancel the effect. It does not offer the wearer of the W.A.R. Suit any advantages, and they may draw additional fire.

Adam's Apples are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Behemoths on Prison Island and Valak Mountain. According to their description, they are made of condensed ether and many scholars are investigating them.
The 1F Main Power Switch (Japanese: , 2F Shudengen Kukaku) is a landmark in . It is located on the first floor of Mechonis Field, south of the 2nd Lift - 1F. It powers the lift on the first floor.
The 3rd Lift - 3F (Japanese: , Dai-3 Rifuto: 4F) is a location in . It is located on the third floor of Mechonis Field, and is powered by the power switch on that floor.
The 3F Main Power Switch (Japanese: , 4F Shudengen Kukaku) is a landmark in . It is located on the third floor of Mechonis Field. It powers the lift on the third floor.

After completing this mission, the Flight Module is added to all Skells owned by the player and to all new Skells. The test Skell is an AS0115 Formula XT, a level 15 version of the Formula light Skell. The equipped weapons and armor cannot be changed but can be removed, kept in inventory and used after the mission. It is registered to Cross for the duration of the test flight. Agniratha (Japanese: , Teito Agunirāta; English dub: ) is an area in located inside the head of the Mechonis. It is the Mechonis Capital. The Machina lived here before the Telethia were ordered by Zanza to destroy them. Many escaped to the Fallen Arm, but the city itself was deserted by all Machina except for Egil and his sister, Vanea.

Amber Fischer (Japanese: , Kohaku no Fisshā) is a Unique Monster in . It can be found at level 27 in Satorl Marsh near the Altar of Fate anytime but with no fog. It can be found on the small island that is nestled inside the other island which is shaped like a backwards letter "C", in front of the waterfalls exiting the Basin Cave. It can drop the Twin Flamii Eggs needed for Preventing Starvation.
The Agul Mountain Range (Japanese: , Aguru sanmyaku) is a location in . It is located on the upper level of Valak Mountain.

Alba Cavanich (Japanese: , Teito Aruba Māgen) is a city in . It is the capital of the Empire of Mor Ardain, and joins directly to Hardhaigh Palace. It is situated on the left shoulder of the Mor Ardain Titan, and is the only Ardainian city visited during the game.

Ambler Stigmas are Flower collectibles in . They can be found in the Land of Morytha, in particular from the five Collection Points between the Ancient People's Driftland and the Blocked Road, the Collection Point located at the bottom of the Collapsed Roadway and south of the Great Wall Tunnel No. 8, the Collection Point located just left of the Fallen Skyscraper, and the Collection Point located to the left of Megaflote Base with a high probability rate. Twelve are needed during the quest Powered-Up Poppi.

The Altar is an object in . It is located in the Corridor of Silence of Prison Island. Dragon King Alcar appears in front of it during Path to the Top, and must be defeated to obtain the Dragon's Eye that must be fitted into the Altar to raise the transporter granting access to the Prison Terrace. Activating the teleporter is the final point of no return in this game.

The Agnus Castle Barbican (Japanese: , Agunusu Jōka Yōsai) is an Area in , located in the Erythia Sea of the Cadensia Region. It is located directly beneath Agnus Castle. The head of the Bionis can be seen behind the facility. This area used to be City territory, and was where the first City stood before its destruction at the hands of N.

Ancient Machines (Japanese: , Kodai Bōeikikō, Ancient Defense Mechanism) are bosses in . They are fought at level 8 in the Cylinder Hangar in Colony 9. Upon reaching the Cylinder Hangar, the party is forced to fight two of them to continue the story. The first Ancient Machine on the left has a higher attack strength while the second one has a higher ether power. In , a third one is fought during World-Changing Whatchamajig.

Apis (Japanese: , Apisu) are a family of flying insect enemies in and . They resemble bees (and "Apis" is the Latin word for bee). Apis are only found in Makna Forest and later at Valak Mountain. Some carry around large objects that appear to be various kinds of rocks.

Argentum (Japanese: , Avaritia) is a group of Titans in . The largest of the Titans, Goldmouth, looks like a flying whale. The Argentum Trade Guild, a mercantile nation, was founded on a ship attached to this Titan, allowing them to navigate it like a balloon. Goldmouth is only large enough to hold the man-made structures of the city; there is little wildlife on the Titan itself. Because it always floats on the surface of the Cloud Sea, it is not affected by the tides.

They increase the duration of the current Driver and Blade Combo by up to 35% when switching to a combo-requesting Blade. Combo-requesting Blades are Blades that have the ability to further one of the currently active combos, and are identifiable by their face icons being highlighted with a blue pulsating effect. When performing a Blade Switch to one of these, the timer gauge for all active combos will briefly pause. Due to an error in its programming, this accessory produces no effect.
Ansels (Japanese: , Anseru) are an enemy family in the . They are a flying enemy type of similar size and power to Rhoguls.

Aura Antols (Japanese: , Aura Antoru) are enemies in . They are members of the Antol family, and can be found at level 53 at the Transformer Area, 5th Pulse Zone, as well as Digit 1, in Fallen Arm. Four of them must be defeated for Powerless. They can drop the Silver Antol Fibres needed for Power Up!.

Asana, the Azure Star (Japanese: , Hoshiao no Āsana) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Cervus family. It can be found at level 30 at Lake Ciel in Sylvalum. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Asana, the Azure Star.

The Armed Destroyer Galdr (Japanese: , Sentō Kuchiku-gata Garudora) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Galdr machine. It can be found at level 45 at the Ruined City of O'rrh Sim in Cauldros.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Arms Attachments (Japanese: , Āmuzu Atatchimento) are accessories in . They increase the attack power of Mech Arms-class weapons by up to 29%. This boosts their Auto-Attack stat during combat, increasing all damage dealt while using them. This attack power increase can stack with the effects of the Master Attachment accessory.

Armu Retrieval (Japanese: , Aruma no Hokaku) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 2 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 50 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 12 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Superstrength", "Transport Mastery" and "Earth Mastery" Field Skills.

Barbaric Sitri (Japanese: , Bankō no Shitorī) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Antol family, and can be found at level 47 in the Antol Den on Valak Mountain. It is one of the targets of The Balance of Power. It drops Soya Paste Shells, two of which are needed for Cook-Off Showdown!.

Avalanche Abaasy (Japanese: , Sekkan no Abāshi) is one of the five Superbosses in . It is a Unique Monster and a member of the Dragon family; it can be found at Three Sage Summit on Valak Mountain after the events of the Mechonis Core (Chapter 17). It spawns only at night, during a blizzard. Like all dragons in the game, it will appear by flying down to the ground when the party is near or at where it spawns. It can drop the Demonic Everflame needed for Replica Monado 4. At level 120, it is the highest level enemy in the game.

Banquet Vassago (Japanese: , Enraku no Wasago) is a quest exclusive Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Chilkin family, and it can be found at level 48 in the Antol Den on Valak Mountain during The Balance of Power after hatching from the large Bonterra Pod. It can drop an Aged Chilkin Hair, which is needed for A Token of Friendship. The Antol Den is located above the Nopon Camp inside the Hollow Bone. To reach it, the party must slide through the Hollow Bone, jumping over the first and second gaps, and land on a ledge; Quick Step gems and light armour may be needed to reach the ledge.

Bana the Betrayer (Japanese: , Uragiri no Bа̄n) is a quest in . It can be received from Gadada at the Pollen Works in Frontier Village. It becomes available after completing the Mechonis Core. To receive this quest, Destroying the City Trade must have been completed before the events at the Mechonis Core.

The Battle Effects, often referred to as Buffs and Debuffs, are a battle mechanic in . During battles, several strengthening and weakening effects can occur that can change a character's stats, abilities, and behavior, and their activations depend on the Arts used, the surrounding Battle Probes installed, and the ongoing Weather effect.

Automaton Sentries are enemies in . They are Levnises used by the Lost Numbers, and can be found at level 6 in Alfeto Valley during Chapter 1. More are fought as Quest Exclusive Enemies during Choices at level 54 at Vinisog Holm in Erythia Sea and during Life in the City at level 50 in the Caelum Residential Quarter in the City.

Benign Crickets (Japanese: , Ryuuseisuzumushi) are collectables in . They can be found in Makna Forest. According to their description, they fly like shooting stars and a moving swarm of them are known as 'Meteors'. Four are required for Honouring the Nopon Sage.

Befalgar Pedestal (Japanese: , Befaruga no Daiza) is a Secret Area in . It is located on the upper level of Valak Mountain. During Believing Again, the party is required to collect the Morning Dew Ice, which can be found here at dawn, or 5:00. The area also must be explored during Valak Mountain Research. The area is a simple slab of stone with no additional markers. Its origin and purpose are unknown, although by its name and design it is likely linked to the Giants. There are no enemies here.

The Bionis' Wrist (Japanese: , Kyoshin no tekubi) is a landmark in . It is located on the lower level of Valak Mountain. It connects the mountains with Sword Valley. After reaching the end of the Mechonis Field, a rockslide will block the cave, making the areas that come after the wrist inaccessible.

Colony 15 is a Kevesi Colony in , located at Hargan Point in Erythia Sea. Its Consul is Triton, who is also its Commander. After completing A Young Noble's Request, the members of Colony 15 relocate to the City. During Colony 15 Soldiers Missing, it is revealed that Colony 15 has joined the Lost Numbers, with Triton being allowed in the City after the quest's completion.

Cruz Paguls are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Pagul family, and can be found at level 33, day or night, at Latael Shore, on the island below Hovering Reef 5, on the Secluded Island and at Anu Shore, all at Eryth Sea. They have a tendency to dig at the ground, likely in search of small insects to devour. Five of them need to be defeated to complete Alcamoth's Monster Quest 1 - Part 1. They can drop the Pagul Hot Pots needed for Losing the Taste for Alcohol.

The Cryptic Sign (Japanese: , An'noun Sain, Unknown Sign) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a fork-like symbol made of small rocks located in Oblivia, atop a large rock promontory northeast of FN Site 306. It is normally accessible by Skell with the Flight Module, but an exploit makes it fairly easy to ascend in a Skell without flight. It is almost solely inhabited by Saltats. As with all Unexplored Territories, its discovery yields an achievement ("The Enigmatic Cryptic Sign").

Dadaan, the Strongest Prone (Japanese: , Baiasu Saikyō no Dadān) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Ganglion Prone. He can be found at level 77 at Scabland Fortress next to FN Site 307 in Oblivia, accompanied by The Dadaan Girls, after completing Chapter 12. Dadaan has the ability to instantly destroy all Skells being piloted by the party if the player uses them during the battle for more than 10 seconds with his signature Art, Absolute Demolisher 2056, although this can be avoided if the player happens to enter cockpit mode right before the attack is unleashed. Cooldown is a game mechanic in and . It prevents the player from using one art several times in a row endlessly. Once an art is used, it will be greyed out. This is a sign that the art is in cooldown. If you observe the art icon carefully, progressing upwards, the art will slowly start to turn a lighter shade of grey. When the lighter shade reaches the top of the art, the art has finished cooldown and can be used again. The more powerful the art, the longer the cooldown generally takes, however using Art Points (APs) to upgrade arts will, as well as increasing the power or effect time, reduce the time needed for cooldown (measured in seconds). Corne Island (Japanese: , Korunu-tō) is a Location in . It is an island in Erythia Sea.

Dedeba (Japanese: , Dabōru) is a Nopon in . He can be found in the Pollen Orb Storehouse in Frontier Village. He is Chief Dunga's advisor, and a pawn of Bana who is initially thought to be the kingpin of the Secret Club involving making Red Pollen Orbs into food and drinks. Once Adviser Hunt has been accepted, he cannot be found any more in Frontier Village. During Destroying the City Trade, Dedeba can be found at the Secret Club in Alcamoth. Once this quest has been completed, Dedeba will definitively disappear so it will be impossible to meet him again in the same playthrough.

Dakuku (Japanese: , Daruku) is a Nopon in Xenoblade Chronicles. He is a Nopon Researcher, and can be found in the Nopon Camp on Valak Mountain. He is worried about the state of the mountain's ecosystem; namely that the Antols, under the leadership of Barbaric Sitri, are becoming a threat when they captured the Chilkins along with their leader.

The Damaged Transporter (Japanese: , Kowareta Ten'i Sōchi) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of Prison Island, and is accessed via the Bridge of Grief. This area was where the High Entia Transporter originally was, before the Bionis' Awakening on the former Prison Island area. The Ageless Moabit can be found here. This landmark place, along with the Bridge of Grief have absolutely no music playing in the background, except for battling enemies.

Deadsight Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Six Stars Sniper Rifle. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission The Queen Is Dead. The Deadsight weapons available in-game are: * Devastator Deadsight * Foxfire Deadsight * Rectifier Deadsight * Rugged Deadsight * Sparrow Deadsight

Deadsight II Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Six Stars Sniper Rifle. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission The Duel (Part I). The Deadsight II weapons available in-game are: * Devastator Deadsight II * Foxfire Deadsight II * Rectifier Deadsight II * Rugged Deadsight II * Sparrow Deadsight II

Damage Link is a Status Effect in and . Whenever a character affected by this debuff is damaged, nearby allies of that character will take the same amount of damage as they had. The amount of damage relayed is unaffected by equipment that increases debuff power; instead increasing debuff power only increases the radius over which damage is shared.
Dark Draiguls are Normal Enemies in . They are Fogbeast Draiguls and can be found at level 47 at Prison Island on the Black Mountains during Red Lightning.
Dark Egels are Normal Enemies in . They are Fogbeast Egels, and can be found at level 47 at Prison Island on the Black Mountains.

Dark Garaffas are Normal Enemies in . They are Fogbeast Garaffas, and can be found at level 40 around the Gelgemos Garrison at The Ragmos Desolation, at level 52 at the Sullied Temple of Abitalia on the Aurora Shelf, and at level 42-46 at the Belgazas' Drifts and on Prison Island, respectively, on the Black Mountains.

Dark Feris are Normal Enemies in . They are Fogbeast Feris, and can be found at level 51 at the Sullied Temple of Abitalia on the Aurora Shelf, and at level 42-46 at Belgazas' Drifts and Prison Island on the Black Mountains.

Dark Skwarors are Normal Enemies in . They are Fogbeast Skwarors, and can be found at level 40 around the Fallen Gate of Ulcaria and Raguel Bridge - North on The Ragmos Desolation, at level 41-45 at Belgazas' Drifts and Prison Island on the Black Mountains, and at level 50 at the Sullied Temple of Abitalia on the Aurora Shelf.

Dark Laias are Normal Enemies in . They are Fogbeast Laias, and can be found at level 53 at the Sullied Temple of Abitalia on the Aurora Shelf, and at level 40-45 on Prison Island on the Black Mountains.

Development Levels, or Dev Levels, are a mechanic in . It measures a nation's level of economic development and the reputation of the player, similarly to Area Affinity in . The mechanic only exists for areas which have significant populations, including the Argentum Trade Guild, Gormott Province, Kingdom of Uraya, Empire of Mor Ardain, Leftherian Archipelago, Indoline Praetorium and Kingdom of Tantal. The Development Level of an area affects the price of goods purchased at shops in the area. At 0 stars, the purchase price of any shop items are twice their sell prices (which is a fixed constant). Dettl Paguls (Japanese: , Ditēru Pagūru) are enemies in . They are level 34–38 members of the Pagul family, and can be found when salvaging at Lascham Island or Torigoth Flower Patch in the Gormott Province. They can also be found when salvaging at the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild during the quest Bana's Secret Treasure.

Duoguills (Japanese: , Guira) are flying piscinoids in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They look like flying sharks with electric tentacles. They are primarily nocturnal creatures, and only use electric attacks. They can be found in Primordia, Oblivia, and Sylvalum.

Dragons (Japanese: , Doragon, lit. "European dragon") are the strongest family of monsters in and . They possess a lot of power, and can be very difficult to defeat. They are structurally similar to Sauroses. There are only three dragons in plus one in . They are as follows: * The first, Dragon King Alcar, is a level 79 boss encountered in Prison Island, triggered by the Dragon Summon. * The second one, Demon King Dragonia, is a level 99 quest exclusive enemy. It is found during Defend Colony 6 - Demon which is triggered by having 90% of Colony 6 restored. Emperor Beetles (Japanese: , Suoukanabun) are collectables in . They can be found on Prison Island. According to their description, they are stocky beetles whose red colouring and ferocity are second to none.

The Ether Crystal Deposit (Japanese: , Ēteru Kesshō Saikutsujō) is a location in . It is clifftop area located in the Eryth Sea, connected by teleporter to Hovering Reef 6, which it is south-east of. It can be accessed by Skip Travelling to Hovering Reef 4, then teleporting to Hovering Reef 5, then to Hovering Reef 6, and finally to the Ether Crystal Deposit.

Energy for Remodeling (Japanese: , Kaizōyō Enerugī) is a Merc Mission in . It is received in Tora's House in the Gormott Province during the Blade Quest Powered-Up Poppi. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Industry Mastery", "Mineralogy" and "Mental Arithmetic" Field Skills. It can be used to obtain 50 Volt Batteries with which to fill the charging device used to power up Poppi. The mission is not required to complete the quest, as the machine can also be charged with Dynamo Turbines, Gold Condensers, Digital Filaments and Screw Coils, however each battery grants 30 times more energy than one of th

The Energy Converter is the main Poppi Part item in . It can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ. It is a kind of battery displaying the current energy output and its maximum output, necessary for upgrading Poppi's capacity. Other Poppi Parts such as Element Cores can be augmented by using a certain amount of energy. The Energy Converter must be beforehand have enough capacity to output the energy required. Ether Crystals can be spent in order to increase the Energy Converter's maximum energy output and allow Poppi to upgrade other attributes.
FN Site 213 is a Miranium Deposit in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Noctilum, on a small island above sea level to the east of the Divine Roost. It is only accessible through flight.

FN Site 304 is a Miranium Deposit in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, on the small island within the Yawning Giant, and can normally only be reached by flight, or by gliding through the air with a Hraesvelg. There are no enemies here.
FN Site 310 is a Miranium Deposit in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, on the mountain to the west of Lake Basel. It is basically accessible by using a Skell with the Flight Module.

FN Site 410 is a Miranium Deposit in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum. The sightseeing spot can be found in the segment northwest of FN Site 410, by flying aboard a Skell to the very top of the large arches. It activates near the middle, but it feels like it is on the backside, toward the ocean.

The FILE-USP0560GG is a Schematic in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This item is obtained in the middle of the waterfall that falls down from the Divine Roost in Noctilum (the Field-Skill mechanical level 5 and flight capability are required). This schematic can be used to craft a level 50 Skell Superweapon Electric-Flood at the AM Terminal.

Face Nemesis (Japanese: , Feisu Nemeshisu), also known as Silver Face, is a Faced Mechon in . She is the Mechon controlled by Meyneth after Fiora is killed by Metal Face. She wields twin swords and, like other Faced Mechon, has the ability to fly.

The First Sanctum (Japanese: , Dai-1 Seigushitsu) is a location in . It is located off the elevated walkway around the Central Hall of Prison Island, and can only be accessed when Prison Island is revisited. It is reached by proceeding from the Kitchen to the Pillar Control and dropping onto the Bone Pillar. If the Bone Pillar is in the raised position, the party must then jump off the north or south end of the pillar into a pool of water below; otherwise the party can walk along the pillar to these pools. The Abnormal Clone Barg can be fought here.

Fire Elements are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from Ucan Nebulae and the Moonlight Paimon in Valak Mountain. Fire Elements are also available via overtrade with Zain. According to their description, they are fire elements that burn forever when they are put in a furnace.

The Fief of Forgetfulness (Japanese: , Bōkyaku no Hōchi) is a Secret Area in . It is an island located on the Lower Level of the Empire of Mor Ardain, directly beneath the capital Alba Cavanich, and accessible only during low tide via the underside of Midorl Bridge. It's accessible from Kedeigh Gate by taking a stairwell to the right while exiting the city, and then hoping down a series of ledges until you reach a descending tunnel. Demon-Shell Jacob lies in this place. This area is involved during Tranquility.

Field Devastation (Japanese: , Hatake wo Arasu Mamono) is a Merc Group mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 1 star in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 40 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 10 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Agronomy" and "Electric Mastery" Field Skills.

First Class Freshness! (Japanese: , Sendo ga Daiichi!) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 4 stars in Development Level. It will only become available after visiting the Indoline Praetorium for the first time. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Ichthyology" and "Transport Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards store contracts that unlock the following wares: * Leftherian Life in Nopox Hobby Store * Full Moon Eyeliner in Cleo's Cosmetics

It also features a "hover mode", in which the Follow Ball will fly up into the sky and give the party a bird's eye view of their surroundings. It is first introduced by Tatsu when the party meets him. It was initially known as the Navigation Ball or Nav Ball.

The Floating Reef (Japanese: , Fuyū Ganshō) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a floating island located in the sky above Lake Basel in Oblivia, and can only be reached by flight. The FN Site 320 is located here, as are several Treasure Boxes. Aerozium must be found here during Fitting In. Chiroro and Dadato can be found here before Unsatisfied Customer and during Mia Grows Up respectively.

Fonsa Myma (Japanese: , Shuto Fonsu Maimu) is a city in . It is the capital of the Kingdom of Uraya, located inside the Stomach of the Urayan Titan. A stairway leads up to the Olethro Ruins. There are no enemies here except during quest and story events. In , the surviving ruins of Fonsa Myma, known as the Ruins of Seebu, can be found inside the Urayan Tunnels. Over time, almost the entire city's land has since collapsed into a chasm beneath the dead Titan. All that remains are Sevind Palace Plaza, the Holy Gate of Fontana, and the two large towers that stood in front of them, but all four of the staircases connecting the former two landmarks (including the Great Stairway and the Old Pilgrim

The Fonsett Waters (Japanese: , Iyasaki Kaiiki) is a level in . It is the Cloud Sea and smaller islands surrounding Fonsett Island in the Leftherian Archipelago. Bridges through the Cloudway link it to Rigitte Waters. Ysheva Harbor, a port that links the archipelago to Indol, is located here.
Fleecyflossy is an NPC in . She is a Nopon who can be found on the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild. She must be spoken to during Powered-Up Poppi.

Flying Flounders are Fish collectibles in . They can be found in the Empire of Mor Ardain, in particular from the two Collection Points in the Nopon Pioneers' Spring. In the , Flying Flounders can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo. Two are required for Vess to make Puri Leaf Dumplings once she has Level 4 "Dumpling Pro" skill. Two are also needed to cook Pyra's Meatball Pot-au-Feu and three to cook Pyra's Baked Redfish at Tora's House or Corinne's House after obtaining the Fire Dragons Recipe from the DLC Quest Midnight Feasting upon installing the New Quests Pack 1 of the Expansion Pass.

Flying Monsters (Japanese: , Tobimawaru Monsutā) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 3 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 1 hour, but it can be reduced down to 15 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Leaping", "Wind Mastery" and "One Lucky Gal" Field Skills.

Flying Fortress Desmor (Japanese: , Hikō Senkan Desumorasu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Moramora family and can be found at level 55 flying above the Dannagh Region and the Aletta Region. It spawns at and is most easily engaged around the south eastern edge of the Turqos Plateau. Notably, it is the only red Moramora seen in the .

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Getting a Member's Card (Japanese: , Kaiinshō wo Teniirero) is a Timed Surprise Quest in . It is automatically triggered in Alcamoth during the course of Destroying the City Trade, that is received from Gadada in Frontier Village.
The GF Main Power Switch (Japanese: , 1F Shudengen Kukaku) is a landmark in . It is located on the ground floor of Mechonis Field, and provides power to the 2nd Lift - GF.

The Full Moon Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission First Class Freshness!. It enables the purchase of Full Moon Eyeliners from the Cleo's Cosmetics shop at Goldmouth in the Argentum Trade Guild.

Galactic Flight (Japanese: , Seiun Kishō) is a Chain Art in . It is Fiona's Chain Art during a Chain Attack. During this Chain Art, in addition to granting Power Charge to all allies, she charges the Chain Attack gauge, allowing for additional Chain Orders to be activated. On Normal and Hard difficulty, this charge is sufficient for one extra order; on Easy, it allows for two extra orders instead due to the increased Chain Attack gauge gain on that difficulty.

Glory Slobos (Japanese: , Gurōrī Sorobosu) are enemies in . They are members of the Slobos family, and can be found at level 97 at the Three Sage Summit on Valak Mountain. They drop the Yellow Slobos Rock required for Replica Monado 5. In the beginning of battle they will give themselves a buff that increase strength but lowers defense, or vice versa.

Glaive Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Six Stars Longsword. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission The Unbreakable Sword. The Glaive weapons available in-game are: * Audacious Glaive * Bewitched Glaive: Blood Dance * Bewitched Glaive: Receding Rust * Ethereal Glaive: Helldragon * Faithful Glaive * Intrepid Glaive * Masterstroke Glaive * Mighty Glaive: Galaxy Chief * Pulverizing Glaive * Signature Glaive: Allegiance * Signature Glaive: Fledgling * Signature Glaive: Four Virtues * Steelbreaker Glaive * Godbreaker Glaive * Phenomenon Glaive

Glowing Retinas are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Tored Ageshus on Prison Island. Glowing Retinas are otherwise unavailable. According to their description, they are retinas that shine constantly with a glow that is like moonlight.

Godsford Isle (Japanese: , Kamiwatashi no Shima) is a landmark in . It is located in the Fonsett Waters of the Leftherian Archipelago, between the Isle of Urchon, Island Base Lindwurm, and Lud Cloudway: Fonsett. It is above the Isle of Terminomni. The ceiling of the island can be reached by taking a running leap from the slope between the Isle and the Cloudway, and has the Unique Monster Rapturous Scandia living atop it as well as the Sealstone of Air required for A Real Challenge. There is a Salvage Point here.

The Graduation Certificate is a Key Item in . It is needed to complete the quest Powered-Up Poppi. It is given to Poppi by Fleecyflossy after defeating the Torl Marrin on the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild.

Godlike Krastor (Japanese: , Kassatsujizai no Ganryuu, Ganryu of the Power of Life or Death) is a Unique Monster in . They are an Agnus Soldier, and can be found at level 82 alongside Impregnable Sandhu at the Ruins of Seebu in the Urayan Tunnels. They form the "Agnian Assassins" duo with Impregnable Sandhu. The Large-Scale Shock Skill can be earned by the Soulhacker class by defeating them.
The Goods for the City are a Key Item in . They are provisions intended for the City that were stolen by Gulkins and later retrieved during Why So Busy?.

Gondorl Cathedral (Japanese: , Gondoa Daiseidō) is a landmark in . It is located on the fifth floor of Prison Island. It leads into the Corridor of Silence, where there is a transporter that teleports the party into the point of no return, which is the final cutoff point in the game. In , a Time Attack portal can be found to the north of the entrance here.

The Great Makna Falls (Japanese: , Makuna Daibakufu) is a location in . It is located in Makna Forest. It is found in the southwest portion of the map, and is an enormous waterfall. There is a large lake here, with a lone island in the middle. The lake is connected to the river which the bridges cross over. A rainbow can be seen at Great Makna Falls between 12:00 and 14:00. The Divine Sanctuary directly overlooks the Falls, and the Lakeside is on the northern shore. There is a small unnamed island in the middle of the lake, which Unreliable Rezno can be found on during the day. The Pure Perfume needed for one route of Looking for Freedom can be found here.

Guldos are a family of enemies in . They are dark gray humanoids with glowing blue growths found only in the Land of Morytha. Guldos come in three varieties; small blueish ones, larger reddish ones and gargantuan blueish ones. Guldos were once humans who tried to replace their brain cells with Core Crystals in an attempt at immortality after the world was left in ruins. The experiment had mixed results; they were corrupted and transformed into horrible mockeries of their own selves, but they successfully managed to survive for millennia, obtaining healing capabilities similar to that of a Blade.

|-|XC3 = |-|FR = Greedstones are Gemstone Collectibles in and . They can be found in the Aetia Region in . They can also be produced from the Hillside Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They can be found on the Black Mountains in . Four are needed for the Black Mountains Collectopaedia.

Gruth is an NPC in . Gruth is an Ardainian who appears on the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild as part of Fleecyflossy's quiz during Powered-Up Poppi, alongside Beltran and Cheelo. Gruth is one of the incorrect options in the quiz.

Gravina Bridge (Japanese: , Gurabina-bashi) is a location in . It is located on the fourth floor of Prison Island, and is a bridge that spans the Great Canyon. It connects two teleporters; one links to the Arena, the other to the Gondorl Cathedral. There is a Heart-to-Heart - "Untold Feelings" - at the north end of the bridge.

Harict Chapel (Japanese: , Harikuto raihaidō) is a landmark in . It is located on the lower level of Valak Mountain. It is the Sealed Tower which Alvis led the party towards when they first arrived at Valak Mountain. There is a Heart-to-Heart - "In Ose Tower" - inside.

The Heart Entrance (Japanese: , Kyoshin no Shinzō Iriguchi) is a landmark in . It is located in the Bionis' Interior. During the story progression, Lorithia awaits for the party inside. After defeating her a dark portal appears at the center. It is this portal that teleports the party into the sunken Prison Island, which is otherwise inaccessible.

Hartmut, the Calamity (Japanese: , Taika no Harutomūto) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Millepod and can be found at level 91 around the cliffs in the southeastern part of the Yawning Giant in Oblivia. It is the most powerful enemy in Oblivia. Killing it is required for segment recon. As Hartmut flies above a bottomless pit, Skells are all but mandatory to fight it. It is possible to wait for Hartmut to fly over to the land bridge near Mesa Fortress, but doing so takes a long time.

Heidl Taos (Japanese: , Haideru Taōsu) are enemies in . They are members of the Taos family and can be found at level 51-53 around the Cliffs of Morytha. Because they often fly around far out of range, it can be difficult to engage them. The easiest one to fight is just north of Balquors Ruins. Four of them must be defeated to unlock Brighid's level 4 Will-o'-the-Wisp, Aegaeon's level 4 Midnight Mist, and Perdido's level 4 Diamond Flight Blade Specials, while five are suggested to be defeated to unlock Finch's level 4 Blast of Fresh Air, and Azami's level 4 Nightmare Rondeau Blade Specials.
Heal Harmony is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Signifer class that sets a field granting a Regenerate effect, healing 50% of user's Healing Power to allies in the field every two seconds.

Hovering Reef 8 (Japanese: , Dai 8 Fuyū Ganshō) is a location in . It is one of the Hovering Reefs, and is located above Eryth Sea. It connects to Hovering Reef 9, Central Seal Island, and Soltnar Seal Island.

Hovering Reef 10 (Japanese: , Dai 10 Fuyū Ganshō) is a location in . It is one of the Hovering Reefs, and is located above Eryth Sea. It connects to Central Seal Island, Khatorl Seal Island and the Ether Plant.

The High-Velocity Lift (Japanese: , Hidari Daitaikotsu Kōsoku Rifuto, lit. Left Thighbone High-speed Lift) is a location in . It is located on the fourth floor of Mechonis Field, directly west of the Upper Bulkhead Bridge. Activating it is the objective of the story quest The High-Velocity Lift, and once it is activated, five minor enemy Mechon will spawn in front of it, guarding the entrance. It goes up to the fifth floor, where Jade Face is fought.

The High Entia Transporter (Japanese: , Haientā Ten'i Sōchi) is a landmark in . It is located on the ground floor of Prison Island. It is the first landmark encountered on Prison Island, and is the transporter to and from Eryth Sea. It becomes the Damaged Transporter on a modified area after the Bionis' Awakening.

Hostile Gazes (纏わり付く視線, Searching Glance) is a Field Track in and , composed and arranged by ACE+. It is track 14 of disc 3 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This music is heard whenever an enemy initiates a battle against the party in the Bionis areas of the game: Colony 9, Tephra Cave, Bionis' Leg, Colony 6, Ether Mine, Satorl Marsh, Bionis' Interior, Makna Forest, Eryth Sea, Alcamoth, High Entia Tomb, Prison Island, Valak Mountain, Sword Valley, and the Bionis' Shoulder. This theme is meant to incite the player to either fight or escape.

Highbohn Quadwings (Japanese: , Haibōn Kurōdo) are enemies in . They are members of the Quadwing family and can be found perched during the day, and flying during the night. They are around level 15 - 17 and are located near Singbreeze Bough of Gormott. Its night flight pattern in particular brings it under the bridge connecting Grandarbor's Embrace and Hoary Weald.

Hope's Rest (Japanese: , Kibō no Oka) is a Location in . It is located outside the Agnus Castle Barbican overlooking Erythia Sea. This is where the City was once located, before its destruction at the hands of N. It was a fertile place with lots of crops. This City used to be called "Hope's Rest" by the Citizens. Sometime following its destruction, Agnus took over the territory, with Agnus Castle relocating above here from the Fornis Region. After liberating Agnus Castle, Mio shows Hope's Rest to the rest of the party.
Hollis is an NPC in who can be found in the City. He works as a doctor at the City's Medical Facility.

Hraesvelg (Japanese: , Furesuberugu, Fresberg) is a Skell in . Hraesvelg uses a Japanese sword-like weapon and has a unique form of flight. It was developed by Grenada Galactic Group and its weapons can not be altered, leaving it with set weapons. Its flight form allows a perspective in the cockpit. The level 60 upgrade of this Skell is the Hraesvelg Lord.

The Infernal Crocell (Japanese: , Jigoku no Kurokeru) is a Unique Monster in . It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 58 in Mechonis Field. It is east of the 4F Main Power Switch on the southern side of the platform, although the in-game text for Challenge Quest 2 claims it is "near Power Supply Area 2," it is actually located due north of that area. A nearby level 60 M91/DOGMA may join the battle. The party must defeat the Infernal Crocell to complete the Mechonis Field's Challenge Quest 2 quest received by a Machina in the Garrisoned Troop in the Machina Refuge.

Immortal Mosses are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by the Armoured Rockwell on Bionis' Leg and Satorl Tortas in Satorl Marsh, and are not available for trade. According to their description, they are immortal mosses with a deep eternal greenness. One is needed for the quest Replica Monado 2.

Idea Stats are Stats in that increase the power of newly resonated Blades. Each idea stat can have a maximum level of 10. The levels are increased by collecting idea points obtained when filling up a Blade Affinity Chart. Idea stats influence Blade Resonance. The higher an idea stat is, the more likely the player is to receive a Blade of one of the corresponding elements. When determining the power of a Blade, only the idea stat with the highest level is taken into consideration, unless a Booster is used. If a Booster is used, it will only take into consideration the boosted Idea Stat. Up to five Boosters can be used during each resonance for a single stat, increasing its level to a maximum

|-|XC3 = |-|FR = Ingot Carrots are Vegetable Collectibles in and . They can be found in the Aetia Region in . They can also be produced from the Battlescar Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They can be found on the Black Mountains in . It can also be purchased from the Colony 9 Caravan. Three are needed for the Black Mountains Collectopaedia.
The Island Caravan is a shop in . It is run by a Traderpon and can be found at the Corne Island Camp in Erythia Sea.

Jakt Geyser (Japanese: , Jakuto kanketsusen) is a location in . It is located in the lower region of Valak Mountain, north of the Sealed Tower. It is most likely created by the magmatic current provided by Lava Cave, which is near the geyser. The geyser is strong enough to carry the party all the way up to the upper level of the mountain, near Valak Peak. A Nopon Researcher is found there for the first visit. A few ledges down, the entrance to Hollow Bone can be found. A Heart-to-Heart - "A Snowy Hot Spring" - is located here.

Kana Peak (Japanese: , Kāna-hō) is a location in . It is located on Valak Mountain. It is a peak north of the Mechonis Wound, accessible over a narrow snowy ridge that begins south of Bagnar Snowfield and ends opposite the start of the equally narrow path leading to Befalgar Pedestal. The path does not show up on the map, making it difficult to find without assistance. The party is asked to visit this location during Valak Mountain Research.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Katana Attachments (Japanese: , Katana Atatchimento) are accessories in . They increase the attack power of Chroma Katana-class weapons by up to 29%. This boosts their Auto-Attack stat during combat, increasing all damage dealt while using them. This attack power increase can stack with the effects of the Master Attachment accessory.

Kalukalu is an NPC in . He is a Nopon merchant who appears on the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild as part of Fleecyflossy's quiz during Powered-Up Poppi, alongside Lulumu and Yatata. Kalukalu must be chosen in order to progress.

Kromar Coast (Japanese: , Supikaru no Rigan) is a location in . It is located in Eryth Sea, directly south of Soltnar Seal Island. It is most easily reached by teleporting there, jumping off and swimming out to the coast. As its name implies, the area is almost solely inhabited by Kromars of levels 83-85, making it a good leveling area for a late-game party. On the end of the west upper part of the coast, across the bridge, the Stormy Belagon can be found. Behind it, there is a sealed door that can be opened if the party has obtained the High Entia Emblem.

Kintrees (Japanese: , Oyako no Ki, Parent-and-Child Trees) is a Scenic Viewpoint in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is an elevated plateau with three trees on it located in Oblivia. It is reachable by careful Skell jumping, or more easily by flight from FN Site 315, heading south to the top of the large rock between two mountains. There are usually no enemies here, although several Mission Exclusive Enemies appear here during A New Life.

L-002 Space Analyzers (Japanese: , Kūkan Bunsekikei L-002) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia. Four are required for Yardley's Scheme. This item is most common on the islands' beaches north of the continent.

The Land of Morytha (Japanese: , Morusu no chi, lit. The land of Mors) is a ruined nation in . It is located below the Cloud Sea, near the roots of the World Tree. It was destroyed long before Alrest even existed, and is said to have been the birthplace of the Architect. Once the home of an advanced human civilization, during the events of , it is a ruined city filled with Guldo.

Lascham Island (Japanese: , Rasukamu Ritō) is a landmark in . It is located on the far right side of the upper level of the Gormott Province. The Mokmo Onion can be unearthed here during The Supply Situation. There are two Treasure Troves here. 500 years prior, Lascham Island was known as Lascham Peninsula.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Knuckle Attachments (Japanese: , Nakkuru Atatchimento) are accessories in . They increase the attack power of Knuckle Claws-class weapons by up to 29%. This boosts their Auto-Attack stat during combat, increasing all damage dealt while using them. This attack power increase can stack with the effects of the Master Attachment accessory.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Lance Attachments (Japanese: , Ransu Atatchimento) are accessories in . They increase the attack power of Megalance-class weapons by up to 29%. This boosts their Auto-Attack stat during combat, increasing all damage dealt while using them. This attack power increase can stack with the effects of the Master Attachment accessory.

La Luz Temple (Japanese: , Ra Rūsu Shinden) is a Secret Area in . It is located on the Black Mountains, and becomes accessible during the quest Snow Man's Treasure, via an Ether Lift from the Town of Banerro Ruins. Presumably, this temple was formerly La Luz Church from Valak Mountain.

The Lava Cave (Japanese: , Yōgan Dōketsu) is a landmark in . It is located in the lower region of Valak Mountain, north of the Sealed Tower and the Jakt Geyser. It is a series of tunnels ending in a volcanic cave with waterfalls of lava. It is inhabited by Sierra Vangs, Porcu Hoxes, Ucan Nebulae, Noto Feris, the Moonlight Paimon and the Exposure Wolfol. There are two Fire Ether Crystal deposits in the cave.

Leva'el, the Terminus (Japanese: , Shūmatsu no Revaēru) is a Tyrant in and . It is a Xern Ganglion aircraft. It can be found at level 82 over the west Cauldros Waters after Chapter 12 is completed, directly above the island with the Armed Recon Galdr. Leva'el is capable of summoning Sentinel Satellis units to buff itself and temporarily become invulnerable, as well as Galdr and Seidr to attack. It has a move called Apocalypse Wand, which the player is notified of a countdown as it prepares the attack during the course of combat, which takes over 5 minutes, and deals an instant kill to all party members and Skells.

Launch is a debuff in . Launch causes those inflicted to be flung away. Party members generally fly away from the source of infliction, while enemies generally fly straight up. Some Skell Battle Arts inflict Launch as a side-effect of the attack. Enemies can only be Launched if they are of a certain, small size. Launch can be inflicted outside of battle in two ways. The first is by walking over small enemies with a Skell. This will deal damage and engage battle. The second is by coming into contact with a sufficiently large enemy. This will not engage battle.

Ledro Urchons (Japanese: , Retteru Unin) are enemies in . They are members of the Urchon family, and can be encountered at level 36–40 when Salvaging at the Torigoth Flower Patch and Lascham Island Salvage Points in the Gormott Province. They can also be found when salvaging at the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild during Bana's Secret Treasure.

Life's Fading Flame - Holding These Thoughts is a track from and , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track six of disc five from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track six of disc sixteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments in : * Ethel and Cammuravi's fight to the death * Sena and Lanz's attempted sacrifice to try defeating N. * Noah and Mio overpowering N with the Sword of Origin. This song plays during the following moments in : * When Ghondor sacrifices himself to protect Na'el from N during the memory from Origin of the City's destruction. * Matthew's brief reunion with Na'el after she's freed from Alpha's control. *

Lizard Moon Jewels are materials in . They can be dropped by Dorsiar Lizards in Tephra Cave or traded for with various NPCs. According to their description, they are alluring gemstones of great extravagance that emit moonlight. Four are needed for Friendship Tokens.

The Little Garden of Tradition (Japanese: , Denshō no Hakoniwa) is a location in . It is located in the Rigitte Waters of the Leftherian Archipelago, in the northern hexagonal island, north of Merclibay Islet. After completing Sheba's Tea Party 5, a Treasure Trove containing 1,000,000 Gold will appear at this place. Unveiling it requires 12 levels of Superstrength and 6 levels of Keen Eye, while opening it requires 12 levels of Lockpicking and 6 levels of Ancient Wisdom.

Lost Fighters (Japanese: ) are Quest Exclusive Enemies in . They are Lost Numbers enemies, and can be found at level ? at Great Sword's Base in the Cadensia Region during Payback for Treason, in Erythia Sea during Payback for Treason, and Choices, and in the City at level 50 during Life in the City.

Lost Protectors (Japanese: ) are Quest Exclusive Enemies in . They are Lost Numbers enemies, and can be found at level ? at Great Sword's Base in the Cadensia Region during Payback for Treason, and at Erythia Sea during Payback for Treason, and in the City at level 50 during Life in the City.

Lunae Rings are Accessories in . Only one can be obtained per playthrough, from the Legacy of the Seven container on a small island accessible by rope near Corne Island. It is the only Legacy of the Seven accessory not obtainable in .
Lucius is an NPC in . He is a City Survivor found at Belgazas' Drifts on the Black Mountains. After being rescued from a Dark Vollgull, he passes away due to his wounds.

Lulumu is an NPC in . Lulumu is a Nopon who appears on the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild as part of Fleecyflossy's quiz during Powered-Up Poppi, alongside Kalukalu and Yatata. Lulumu is one of the incorrect options in the quiz.

The Magma Rock is a Key Item in . It is required for the Story Quest The Magma Rock, and is obtained by defeating the Conflagrant Raxeal in the Lava Cave on Valak Mountain. The Magma Rock can be used to melt a Thick Ice Wall at several locations on Valak Mountain.

The Ma-non (Japanese: , Ma Non; English dub: ) are a race of beings in . They are not native of Mira but recently arrived on the planet aboard their spaceship. They are said to be peaceful aliens with advanced technological capabilities and, after moving into New Los Angeles, a love for pizza. They have founded the Candid & Credible Arms Manufacturer, specialized in high-defense ground gears and unlocked after Chapter 5. Following Void's return, the Ma-Non actively worked with their New Los Angeles's allies in order to escape Mira's complete destruction from the Dematerialization events caused by the Ghosts, even suppling their own spaceship to become the base for the new White Whale 2. Memory Space (Japanese: , Kioku Kūkan) is the final area in . This area is separate from the world of the Bionis and the Mechonis. It is a space made from a memory of Zanza's original world from before he became a god. Unlike all the other areas in the game, there is no registered map of Memory Space, although a brownish terrain and the landmarks are displayed in the area map radar. After reaching the Prison Terrace on Prison Island and onwards, it will no longer be possible to save the game, therefore it is not possible to save the game anywhere in this area. Memory Space consists of five landmark places. The first four places consist of three Solar system planets, Saturn, Jupiter and Mars,

The Melfica Road Shop is a shop in . It is the lone shop located in Alcamoth. It is the easiest place to find most arts manuals for Melia. After the events at Mechonis Core, this shop will be permanently inaccessible, as well as some items sold therein that cannot be obtained via alternate means. After the events at Prison Island, the shop expands its selection of weapons, armour, and art books. __TOC__ Note: In the following tables, "PI" refers to the events at Prison Island.

Melodious Melons are Vegetable collectibles in . They can only be found at the Argentum Trade Guild, on Goldmouth Flight Deck in the left field to the right of the Skip Travel point (probability 10%), using the Agronomy Field Skill increases the odds. They can be offered to Pekka as food for his Adult Ardun raising the progression bar by five points. One of them is required to make the DLC Pouch item Love Source.

Mercenaries are a class of enemy in . They are similar to humanoid Driver enemies, but are lacking a Blade. They still wield weapons reminiscent to Blade weapons, such as megalances or greataxes. They are sometimes used to make sure Haze cannot overpower them as her power to restrict beings only works on Blades and Titans.
Merto Island (Japanese: , Meruto Kojima) is a location in . It is located in the Fonsett Waters of the Leftherian Archipelago, just south of Fonsett Island.

Monado Purge (Japanese: , Monadobureikā, Monado Breaker) is one of Shulk's Monado arts in and . The colour of the blade turns light green upon activation. Ether particles are charged onto the blade, allowing Shulk to send a wave of Ether particles to the enemy from afar. This art will inflict the enemy with Aura Seal, which removes any active auras and temporarily blocks the enemy's spike and aura activation abilities. It also inflicts Damage which is calculated based on Shulk's current Ether strength and the art's multiplier. Shulk learns this art during the confrontation with the Telethia at the Lakeside in Makna Forest. __NOTOC__

Monado Cyclone (Japanese: , Monado saikuron) is one of Shulk's Monado arts in and . The colour of the blade turns into a combination of white and gold. Ether particles are concentrated into the Monado, allowing Shulk to unleash a column of powerful Ether from the ground. Enemies within the area effect will be damaged by the Ether. Furthermore, any enemies that are inflicted with Break will be Toppled. Shulk learns this art after destroying the Apocrypha Generator. Monado Cyclone is one of the most situational Topple-inflicting arts in the game. Being a Monado art, Shulk only has access to it when his Talent Gauge is at max. It also depletes 100% of the Talent Gauge, and there may be other Mo

Moonlight Paimon (Japanese: , Gekkō no Paimon) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Nebula family, and can be found at level 46 in the Lava Cave on Valak Mountain. It is in the same room in which the party acquires the Magma Rock by defeating the Conflagrant Raxeal and can later encounter the Exposure Wolfol.

Monta Moramoras are enemies in . They are members of the Moramora family, and can be found at level 43 during the day in numerous places on Valak Mountain, including just below Zokhed Pass and near Nagul Waterfall. Defeating two of them is required to complete the Valak Mountain's quest Monster Quest 1. They drop Moramora Meat Pies, three of which are needed for Reversed Tastes.

Mount Edge Peak (Japanese: , Maunto Ejji Chōjō) is a Scenic Viewpoint in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, atop the highest mountain and reachable from FN Site 321 by flight. There are no enemies here, but it must be visited to complete Off the Record (mechanical). As with all Scenic Viewpoints, its discovery yields an achievement ("Climbing Mount Edge Peak").
Moonstar Lipsticks are Cosmetic Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Praximo Cosmetics in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal. They are one of Pandoria's favorite Pouch items.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Muscle Belts (Japanese: , Mukimuki Beruto) are accessories in and . They increase the wearer's Strength stat by up to 22. The Champion Belt accessory offers a stronger instance of this equipment's effect. For a similar multiplicative effect that can stack with this gear, check the Steam Belt, Silver Belt, Ceramic Belt and Beast-Hide Vest accessories. Other sources of Strength apply before this fixed stat bonus.

Moondog (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is one of the arts of the Strategos class. Upon use, the Art creates a field which heals HP equal to 50% of the user's Healing Power for all allies in its area of effect every 2 seconds.

Moyshe is a NPC in . He lives in the City and is friends with Coralie. During The Path I Forge, he and Coralie run into Seeker and the party after Coralie lost her ring. He views people from outside the City as barbarians.
Newgate Laias (Japanese: , Nyūgeito Raia) are enemies in . They are members of the Laia family, and can be found at level 75 flying around the exterior of Prison Island.

Need Power! (Japanese: , Dengen wo Kyōkyūseyo) is a Story Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received automatically once the party reaches the other side of the Upper Bulkhead Bridge while progressing through Mechonis Field and accepts the story quest The High-Velocity Lift.

Noctilum (Japanese: , Yakō no Mori lit. Noctilucent Forest; English dub: ), also known as Nightglow Woods (Japanese: , Yorupikka Mori) to the Nopon, is a region in . It lies to the northwest of Primordia. Noctilum is very reminiscent of a jungle, with lush greenery and murky swamps. Much of the region is bordered by tall crags that separate it from the oceans of Mira, with some lagoons where gaps meet the ocean. __TOC__

The Noctilucent Sphere (Japanese: , Yakōkyū) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a massive spherical tree in southeastern Sylvalum, which can be reached by flight or a precise jumping technique. At night, the sphere's glow can be seen from the northern portions of Primordia and Oblivia. There are no enemies atop the sphere, but the interior contains several powerful creatures.
New Moon (Japanese: , Shingetsujin, Lit. "New Moon Blade") is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when wielding Uchigatana.

The Ocean Radiant is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is one of the four radiants required for Imperial Ceremony Offerings and can only be obtained while this quest is active. It is located on Central Seal Island in Eryth Sea, in the middle of the bridge where the two ramps connect.

O'rrh Sim Castle Ruins (Japanese: , O-Ra-Shīmu Shiroato) is a Scenic Viewpoint in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in central Cauldros, around the southern and western perimeter of the Ganglion Weapons Hangar. It is reachable from FN Site 506 and Ruined City of O'rrh Sim. A teleporter to the Forgotten Mining Frigate above FN Site 506 is located within the castle. As with all Scenic Viewpoints, its discovery yields an achievement ("Upon the O'rrh Sim Castle Ruins").

Nopon Seven-Star Medals are accessories in , made available with the Version 2.2.0 update. They can be purchased from the Nopon Coin X-change for 77 Gold Nopon Coins. Talking to Miibomii after obtaining seven Nopon Seven-Star Medals unlocks Consul N's Armor as a Clothing option for Noah, and the Leisure Time outfits for Noah, Eunie, and Lanz.

Once We Part Ways (別れ、そして…, Parting, And...) is an Event Track in , composed and arranged by ACE+. It is track 17 of disc 2 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. It is also track 11 on the Xenoblade Chronicles Special Soundtrack and track twenty of disc one from the Xenoblade Definitive Edition Original Soundtrack and Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. Overdrives are battle mechanics in . They are also known as OC Gears or Over Clocking Gears in the Japanese version. They are powerful tools for the party, allowing characters to greatly increase their fighting ability. Overdrive battle mechanics are comparable to Chain Attacks in , although there is no time break involved, nor blue lines connecting the party members shown on the screen. During Skell battles, Overdrive can also be activated. Activating an Overdrive consumes 3000 TP, the same as reviving an ally. The initial time upon activation is 10 seconds. The gauge is filled by multiplying the attacks in a limited time, both to reduce the cooldown of the arts, but also to trigger Tertiar

Overclock Buster (Japanese: , ekushīdo basutā, Exceed Buster) is a Talent Art in . It is the Talent Art of the Swordfighter class. It delivers a powerful blow to the enemy. It can inflict heavy damage when an enemy is dazed, so it is more powerful to coordinate with companions who have daze-inflicting arts.

Over the Sinful Entreaty is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track six of disc four from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track six of disc nine from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments: * Indol's intervention of the Urayan-Ardainian conflict in Temperantia. * Indol rises from the Cloud Sea and attacks the Marsanes. * Rex uses his power as the Master Driver to break Amalthus's control over Mythra, Nia, Dromarch, Brighid, and Pandoria. * The party comes up with a plan to undo Amalthus's control over the Titans. * Dagas taunting the Arrogant Behemoth during Lost Kingdom. * KOS-MOS destroying the Blade Bot at the

Peerless Beaufort (Japanese: , Shippū no Kamuri) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Crustip family and can be found at level 49 on Isle of Sleeping Remains on the Rigitte Waters in the Leftherian Archipelago, lying inside a shell at the north of the island. It must be defeated in order to unlock Zenobia's level 4 "Superstrength", Pandoria's level 5 Lightning Force, and Nim's level 5 Organic Automata Affinity Rewards.

Perplexed Stoyan (Japanese: , Meikyū no Shutorōmu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Serprond family and can be found at level 47 on the Little Garden of Tradition island in the Leftherian Archipelago, emerging from the Cloud Sea to the northwest of Daridan's Stack in Rigitte Waters. If not lured to the center of the island, its drops will fall to the bottom of the Cloud Sea, making it impossible to get them. Perplexed Stoyan can summon Dagus Lysaats when using its art "Mega Wave". It must be defeated in order to unlock Azami's level 5 Nightmare Rondeau and Mythra's level 5 Lightning Buster Blade Specials.

Phonex Escort (Japanese: , Fonekusu Yōjinbō) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province by talking to the Yux on the Treetop Path, when the nation has at least 4 stars in Development Level and after the quest A Phonex Tale has been completed. In order to talk to the Phonex and obtain the mission, Nim must be in the party and have her "Phonex Linguistics" Field Skill at level 2. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Superstrength", "Expeditionist" and "Phonex Linguistics" Field Skills.

The Power Pipe Ruins (Japanese: , Dōryoku Paipu-ato) is a location in . It is located south of Ulna Passage on the Fallen Arm, and is where Reyn and Sharla wake up after falling from Galahad Fortress. This is also where the Oath Sword is found, required for The Oath Sword. An Ice Ether Crystal Deposit containing Chill Plus IV and Auto-Atk Stealth IV gems can be found here. After leaving this location, it cannot be reached again until the Mechonis Key is received for completing The Wilted Flower. The key is used to activate the Pressure Control Device west of Ulna Passage, revealing a wall which can be climbed to reach a passage leading to the Power Pipe Ruins.

Power Up! (Japanese: , Pawā Appu) is a quest in . It can be received from Rakzet after completing the quest Powerless. He can be found near the connected land southwest of the Junks in the Hidden Machina Village. If Fiora is in the active party, she will comment.

Powerful Eligos (Japanese: , Aragami no Erigosu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Antol family, and can be found at level 80 on the southern part of Digit 1 on the Fallen Arm. It can drop the Silver Antol Fibres needed for Power Up!.
Power Supply Area 1 (Japanese: , Dai-1 Dengen Kukaku) is a location in . It is located on the fourth floor of Mechonis Field, north east of the 4F Main Power Switch, and is devoid of enemies.

Primordia (Japanese: , Gensho no Kōya lit. Primordial Wilderness; English dub: ) is a region in . It is the continent where the White Whale's Habitat Unit, now New Los Angeles, crash-landed after the Ark Ship was downed by the alien faction pursuing it. It is the first continent visited, being where Cross is awakened by Elma in the prologue. The region features open grassy plains, large bodies of water, and several tall rock formations. The neighboring region of Noctilum lies to the northwest, while Oblivia can be reached from a land-bridge in the northeast. The region of Sylvalum lies to the north across the shallows.

The Primordia Waters (Japanese: , Gensho no Kōya Kinkai) are a region in . These are the waters which surround the north of Primordia between the continents of Primordia and Sylvalum, and contain several islands inhabited mostly by Prone.

The Primeval Meadow (Japanese: , Gensei Hanazono) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, northeast of FN Site 318, above the ravines. It can be reached by a Skell with a Flight Module, but also unconventionally without flight with normal jumping by certain climbing routes.

Poppi α, or Poppi, (Japanese: , Hana Jetto Spāku Mōdo, lit. "Hana Jet Spark Mode", abbreviated , Hana JS or , Hana) is an Artificial Blade in . She was built by Tora, whom she calls "Masterpon", as a robotic companion. She has a powerful metallic body and perfectly practices the Nopon language. Although Poppi is not a natural Blade awakened from a Core Crystal and Tora is not a Driver, they work as a kind of Driver and Blade duo during battle. She originally uses the power of earth with a Tank class, but she can equip wind, ice, and electric element cores through Poppiswap.
Power Swipe (Japanese: , Pawāsuraido Lit. "Power Slide") is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using a Greataxe.
Powerquake (Japanese: , Pawākueiku) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using a Cobra Bardiche. This art recycles Rex's Power Spike.
Power Unimaginable (Japanese: , Kyodaina Chikara, Enormous Power) is a main story quest in . It is recieved from Hugo in the Torigoth Village on Gormott.
Power Ring (Japanese: , Pawāsākuru, Lit. "Power Circle") is a Battle Art in . It is one of the arts of the Medic Gunner class.

Racti Lexos (Japanese: , Rakutī Rekusosu) are minor enemies in . They are members of the Lexos family, and can be found at level 39 on Hovering Reef 9, the island under Hovering Reef 5, and Soltnar Seal Island in Eryth Sea. One Racti Lexos needs to be defeated to complete Alcamoth's Monster Quest 2 - Part 3. They are the only enemies that drop the Old Dragon Spines needed for Collect Quest 2 and the Lexos Beards needed for Material Quest 4.

Proper Bandaz (Japanese: , Jōdō no Bendazu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Pagul family, and can be found at night during shooting stars at Secluded Island at the Eryth Sea. It must be defeated for Alcamoth's Challenge 1 quest. It can drop a Pagul Hot Pot, five of which are needed for Losing the Taste for Alcohol.

Quay Hollows (Japanese: , Kuei Dōkutsu) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a cave located south of Sylvalum's FN Site 414, on a tongue of rock which extends from the cliff face over the ocean. The entrance is guarded by two Howitzer Launcher Zigs and several Highland Jaculs. Nupopon can be found here during The Divine Nupopon. As with all Unexplored Territories, the discovery of Quay Hollows yields an achievement ("Entering Quay Hollows"). This cave is easily accessible by flight but can also be reached by careful Skell jump.

Razer Visigels (Japanese: , Reizu Narukī) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Visigel family, and can be found at level 51-60 on an island far southeast of Slavebird Isle in Cauldros Waters. The island doesn't have a name, nor is it visible on any of the regional maps.

Raidrifle Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Six Stars Assault Rifle. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Leaving the Nest, along with the Wrothian Male holofigure. The Raidrifle weapons available in-game are: * Devastator Raidrifle * Foxfire Raidrifle * Rectifier Raidrifle * Rugged Raidrifle * Sparrow Raidrifle * Ultra Transience Raidrifle

Regideria was a nation in . It is a mysterious old continent kingdom involved during the quests Lost Kingdom and Dagas's Past: Folktales, and narrated in the book The Mystery Continent. Dagas may have come from this ancient nation, or even ruled it, and feels a bond with it, but admits he cannot be certain he came from Regideria at all. It is said to have been located in Temperantia.

The Revelation Hall (Japanese: , Keiji no Ma) is a location in . It is on the second floor of Alcamoth, reachable from the eastern teleporter at the back of the Audience Chamber. It is a small balcony looking out over the city, and the location of Telethia Galvin during A Merciful End.

Revolutionary Bifrons (Japanese: , Kakumei no Bifuronsu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 60 in Mechonis Field, northeast of the 4F Main Power Switch but before the Power Supply Area 1. The party must defeat the Revolutionary Bifrons to complete the Mechonis Field's Challenge Quest 1 received from a Machina in the Garrisoned Troop in the Machina Refuge.

Rhoguls (Japanese: , Rōguru) are flying enemies resembling birds of prey in the . They are similar in size and power to Ansels, but are larger and have different beaks. Their appearance does not change between games.

Robol Pengs (Japanese: , Roboru Pengu) are enemies in . They are members of the Peng family, and are black with white markings. They can be found at level 40-42 on the Lower Level of the Kingdom of Tantal when it is overcast or snowing, specifically along the shores of the large central frozen lake, and on the east shore of the small unfrozen lake south of the Great Pillar Passage. They fly around the area, stopping briefly to perch on a rock near some Chibal Pengs. Five Robol and Chibal Pengs in total must be defeated to unlock Mythra's level 3 Photon Edge.

This boosts their Auto-Attack stat during combat, increasing all damage dealt while using them. This attack power increase can stack with the effects of the Master Attachment accessory.
The Reinz Egel is a Quest Exclusive Boss in . It is a member of the Egel family, and is fought at level 48 in the Third Sanctum of Prison Island on the Black Mountains during Ancient Contraption.

This boosts their Auto-Attack stat during combat, increasing all damage dealt while using them. This attack power increase can stack with the effects of the Master Attachment accessory.

The Secret Club Card is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is needed to gain access to the Secret Club in Alcamoth as part of Destroying the City Trade. It can be obtained from Nelo by completing Getting a Member's Card.

Save Bionis (Japanese: , Kyoshinkai no Hōkai wo Tomeru) is a Story Quest in . It is received automatically while fighting Yaldabaoth in the Mechonis Core. By using his Energy Replenish art, Yaldabaoth summons three Energy Devices and triggers a vision of Yaldabaoth using Bionis Slash X that triggers Save Bionis. The three Energy Devices must be therefore defeated in order to complete this quest. If the Energy Devices are not destroyed within two minutes, Yaldabaoth will use this Bionis Slash X attack and the party will lose. Once the Energy Devices are destroyed and this quest completed, Yaldabaoth will be Dazed, removing his invincibility aura. The vision tags will break as well, thereby gi

The Second Sanctum (Japanese: , Dai-2 Seigushitsu) is a location in . It is located off the elevated walkway around the Central Hall of Prison Island, and can only be accessed when Prison Island is revisited. It is reached by proceeding from the Kitchen to the Pillar Control and dropping onto the Bone Pillar. If the Bone Pillar is in the raised position, the party must then jump off the north or south end of the pillar into a pool of water below; otherwise the party can walk along the pillar to these pools. The Majestic Clone Barg can be fought here.

The Secret Club is a special location in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is located on floor 1F of Alcamoth at night, in one of the circular rooms along the curved western road. It can only be accessed as part of Destroying the City Trade, as a Secret Club Card is needed to get in. There are four Alcamoth citizens inside the club, as well as a High Entia bouncer that refuses entrance to the party until they obtain the Secret Club Card.

The Samaar Federation is an interstellar federation in . They control a radius of around 6 million light-years of space, spanning multiple galaxies. The Federation is made up of many alien races which have a similar physical composition. The Founders of Samaar were the Samaarians, who came from another universe. It is unclear whether they exist in the current Federation, as Luxaar describes the Human race as the "legacy" of the Samaarians. The Samaar Federation homeland is apparently lost. They are constantly at war with the Ghosts, another alien civilization made up of xenoforms whose physical composition is different from the members of Samaar.
